tina.purpose: SSOT architecture model: module/service/contract inventory AND the runtime data plane (carriers, ownership, flows, egress boundary). gate:dataflow enforces model<->disk completeness, single-writer + render-only ownership, and a reality diff against code; gate:calm validates it against the FINOS meeting-intelligence pattern.
tina.principle: P23 — one writer per data carrier; readers never re-derive a producer's data; the model covers every module/service/contract (no drift).

Read-only full diagnostics resolve effective ASR through Identity and probe configured host/container health without inference. Allowlisted repository checks reuse existing gates and write private local logs. ASR configuration uses existing Identity global/account settings APIs with explicit scoped previews and secret-free output. Fresh local setup creates private configuration and new Compose-managed volumes, refuses existing configuration/resources and occupied ports, and reuses deployment plus optional ASR configuration/status verification; it does not install native capture or models. nodes.name: agent-api
nodes.description: unit control-plane; dispatch -> runtime spawn; internal company README and mail template reads are restricted to trusted services. meeting copilot Per-user ChatGPT disconnect keeps TINA/ASR sessions separate. Terminal OAuth state is cancelled locally; authenticated internal Agent API owns profile writes, disconnect and generation checks under the same file lock as token refresh. Credentials stay in the private auth volume; callbacks from a disconnected generation cannot restore an old account. Existing in-flight workers may retain short-lived tokens. Owner-scoped meeting Q&A reads canonical transcript and explicitly selected linked private Wiki documents, validates source IDs, stores source fingerprints, and creates a new Wiki page only after explicit Apply; existing pages and canonical data are never overwritten. Routine files are owner-scoped active private-workspace resources: anchored no-symlink I/O, per-owner serialized reconcile, source SHA preconditions for explicit Edit/toggle/delete, and stable IDs per workspace/file. Delete removes the source before cancelling all related jobs; shared workspace files never grant schedules. Chat dispatch serializes configuration changes per thread in Redis using expiring locks and keyed model-configuration digests under agent:chat-config:*. Raw credentials are never stored in that metadata. An unchanged configuration reuses its warm worker; changed provider, credential or model waits for the previous turn-complete and requests cooperative stop through the existing chat input stream, confirms terminal state through runtime.v1 and replaces the idle workload before pre-delivering and spawning the next turn. Busy or unverifiable refreshes return actionable errors without sending the prompt to an old provider. The existing thread id, output stream and provider-session history are preserved. Bedrock model discovery reads paginated regional foundation-model/inference-profile lists; credential tests use native InvokeModel. The API image packages the same Python provider helpers and automatic thinking policy as the worker. All providers use automatic thinking; legacy effort pins are ignored, and the settings UI exposes no manual thinking field. Worker configuration digests include the deployed provider-adapter revision, so adapter fixes replace old warm workers without discarding conversation history. Gemini defaults to gemini-3.5-flash. Gemini, DeepSeek and Bedrock credential tests verify native function-call/result round trips before reporting success; Bedrock uses the same InvokeModelWithResponseStream protocol as its CLI and decodes complete AWS event-stream frames with checksum validation; custom API model registration supplies exact model IDs to the pinned CLI SDK rather than embedding endpoint URIs. Groq credential tests verify a real function-call/result round trip through the worker request adapter before testing summaries. Model discovery excludes speech-only Orpheus entries and marks known text-only ALLaM as summary-only, preventing chat selection while preserving meeting use. Explicit /research chat commands and document research requests resolve a private writable note destination from the authenticated active set. Private Codex history restores turn-scoped recorded source metadata and original opened URLs; missing reference mappings remain visibly unresolved. Voice API traces use the bot request UUID forwarded in an internal header and carry it as separate worker dispatch metadata. Structured logs include only stages/status, duration and source counts; no source text, questions or credentials. Whole-meeting recaps use the existing three-worker background pool and one 120-second map/select/verify waiting budget. Computation is request-UUID scoped and never returns a partial summary as whole-meeting evidence. Each stage probes the internal owner/service-authenticated Meeting API turn permit before and after inference, in addition to source/policy checks; stopped/replaced turns cannot authorize further stages or late publication. Voice-to-chat sessions resolve a claimed, bounded owner snapshot on every send/reconnect, without ambient full-meeting grounding. Decision Flow adds literal decision content/status extraction and current-room evidence retrieval; decided claims require exact citations plus independent verification, fresh policy/source checks and a current turn before pending draft creation. Draft histories compact only at their bound, keeping the original request and exact snippets proving current fields; confirm/cancel/leave remain available after eight inputs. Task Flow, like Decision Flow, refuses blind retries after an uncertain save. Voice draft review authorization resolves the requested draft ID directly with unchanged owner/meeting/policy/completed-readback checks, independently of the paginated twenty-record list. List responses expose an optional next_offset. Voice Retrieval V2 filters only authorized source snapshots before rank/context expansion: raw BM25 and pinned offline Underthesea Vietnamese BM25 share lexical weight with bounded workspace aliases and low-weight character candidates, then weighted RRF fuses existing E5. Speaker/source-clock time filters narrow candidates; entities are soft rank hints and never identities or permission grants. Original sentence-aware chunks and up-to-two neighboring source turns retain parent fingerprints/offsets and existing quote budgets. Canonical source quotes appear once with compact retrieval-evidence.v2 refs; worker generation refreshes refs after its guarded LLM rerank, and final review/revocation remains unchanged. A separate pinned BGE local safetensors evaluation candidate is offline/explicit and not a default production model or new service. Private evaluation reports add Recall@k/MRR/NDCG@k/latency without approving draft labels. Voice evidence prioritizes explicitly selected direct/Wiki documents within eight returned documents, proving Wiki eligibility from current direct meeting roots with bounded additional discovery; selection alone never grants a path. Voice isolates optional unselected document read errors from independently verified selected evidence. Selected read errors and unresolved Wiki eligibility remain service errors; generic Knowledge reads stay strict. Owner-scoped project voice source selections live atomically in private workspace metadata. Rooms reference immutable profile fingerprints; reads validate profile grants, source paths and meeting ownership. Source-profile removal revokes referenced voice sources. Voice sandbox jobs receive a server-frozen live meeting lease, authorized snapshots and no workspace mounts; model routing follows account settings. New capable Google Meet rooms grant include_workspace_wiki for read-only retrieval of all content Markdown in the owner primary private workspace. Linked-document selection remains available for legacy or opted-out rooms. Whole-Wiki retrieval excludes hidden/symlink/other-account paths, rejects oversized sources and corpus overflow explicitly, and retains bounded excerpts, citation validation and source/policy revocation; it never mounts personal workspaces into a voice harness. Live voice jobs freeze current room leases for both completion and sandbox paths; a cancelable output reader checks the lease every 250 ms and asks runtime to stop only the isolated revoked worker. Interrupted heard history retains a completed spoken prefix with source guards used only for revocation; new answers retrieve evidence again. Public voice answers require original Agent-Reach excerpts and independent verification; provider summaries alone cannot authorize speech. Missing gold product returns the existing spoken clarification. Only a recent heard fixed clarification plus a whitelisted product choice reconstructs public product/side/unit/currency/today slots; no arbitrary history text is exported. Web lookup/final preserve the clarification boolean through the existing room policy checks. The staging Agent API stores workspaces on encrypted EFS. For post-meeting drafts it resolves the authenticated caller's meeting and selected workspace document before dispatch and revalidates both sources before returning the draft. The Terminal pilot scopes jobs to eligible meeting owners and stores the latest job and cited result on EFS. Terminal polls through the authenticated Gateway, and Agent API checks the source permissions again when it serves a completed result.

nodes.name: bot
nodes.description: Spawned-per-meeting worker: join -> capture -> selected ASR -> transcript.v1. Opt-in Google Meet voice reuses original ASR hypotheses before LocalAgreement, accepts local LiveKit WakeWord acoustic calls for TINA ơi/hey TINA, assembles same-channel bounded source-clock questions, fences duplicate/late windows and preserves transcript. Separate native VAD and KWS children; verified answer sentences use shared local TTS plus existing Stop. Owner diagnostics use allowlisted reason codes and at most three ASR prefix words; no full question/provider errors enter logs. Voice-only VAD endpoints advance the same ASR window below minimum/cadence, reuse covered results and serialize uncovered tails without closing/resetting transcript state. Content-free request-correlated timing logs separate acknowledgment from answer playback and preserve source clocks. Voice onset is distinct from retained pre-roll, and buffer generation/deferred-close fences run before hypothesis observation. Receive audio uses a separate meeting_rx sink; tts_sink feeds an always-available virtual_mic source. TTS sink mute plus verified Meet UI gate speech; system source mute is never used as a speech gate. Playback requires observed meeting microphone state after a bounded single-toggle verification and bounded device-recovery wait; blocked or unknown state fails closed. Bounded content-free audio counters observe the unchanged capture tee and same ASR requests; per-frame telemetry never adds HTTP calls. Opt-in NS runs after original archive taps and before both ASR and Silero. Off is synchronous bypass; timeout/overload/error drains only unacknowledged raw packets once, fences late outputs, and exposes failed mode. Capture stops before NS drain and ASR finalization. Voice timing separates acknowledgment, waiting notice and answer request, first PCM, prebuffer and local microphone injection. The playback receipt requires verified meeting mic, player spawn and successful first PCM write; it does not prove remote audibility. First-answer timestamps survive lookahead; logs contain no text or credentials. Optional shadow-only Smart Turn v3.2 CPU INT8 plus Namo v1 Multilingual INT8 run in a separate native process per new voice bot. Shared checksum-pinned model/tokenizer assets mount read-only. The controller submits same-caller <=8s audio and ASR text after covered VAD endpoints; it never waits for or acts on scores. Private text/audio remain bounded memory/IPC; logs contain scores, UUID/channel/timings only. Stop, resumed speech and identity/source gaps fence late observations. A 1.5-second optional inference timeout retires only the observer. LiveKit keeps manual turn control and existing ASR/transcript ownership is unchanged. Microphone UI operations have a five-second caller deadline while the underlying evaluate queue stays serialized; timed-out unmute cannot release PCM and new playback requires verified mute recovery. Remote cancellation and heard-prefix receipts proceed independently of a stalled mic UI. Pre-admission cleanup always stops the TTS sink, but skips meeting microphone DOM access until an unmute was attempted. Once attempted, Stop retains strict mute verification, queue serialization and late-playback fencing. Anonymous Google Meet joins recognize the exact Continue as guest choice before name entry, click it once with the existing UI driver, and share the original selector deadline; authenticated identity and refusal checks remain authoritative.

nodes.name: transcription
nodes.description: transcription — OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions boundary with selectable backends: faster-whisper/CTranslate2, Apple MLX/Metal, and loopback FunASR Qwen3-ASR with FSMN-VAD. Clients send bounded audio windows, continuity prompts and content-free capture-lag metadata. FunASR exposes asr-status.v1 with actual device, bounded request timing samples, queue and model percentiles; Terminal reads it through a verified admin proxy. Browser render timings remain local. Does not write any redis carrier (the bot XADDs segments). Optional native Rust backend runs Silero VAD and Qwen3-ASR-0.6B INT8 through sherpa-onnx on CPU at host loopback :18001; it preserves VAD segment offsets and the same ASR status contract. The FunASR adapter forwards min_silence_duration_ms to FSMN max_end_silence_time (100-2000 ms, default 800 ms, explicitly pinned), preserving per-VAD sentence offsets for downstream alignment. An isolated single-source Apple Silicon PoC under deploy/transcription/streaming-poc validates real Qwen Transformers decoder token callbacks and paced growing-window hypotheses on cached VI/EN evaluation clips. It is not a selected production endpoint, does not claim an incremental audio encoder, and never changes/restarts production services; private external artifacts record token timing, accuracy, RAM and before/after listener identities. Sub-200 ms FunASR inputs receive trailing silence only in the temporary inference file to avoid incomplete FSMN frames; source PCM, reported duration and sentence bounds retain the original source interval. Empty input and inference failures remain errors. Optional native VieGem-ASR + KenLM endpoint at loopback :18005 uses separately pinned VieGem and EmbeddingGemma 2 assets, PyTorch FP32 on explicit MPS/CPU/CUDA, FSMN on CPU and upstream 4-gram CTC prefix beam decoding. It uses a shared authenticated bounded HTTP worker; inference is serialized and source VAD offsets stay on the original timeline. Installation does not select the endpoint globally. No incremental streaming, word alignment or automatic transcript polish is claimed; VieGem use is restricted by its non-commercial research license and Gemma terms. Identity also exposes the named viegem backend: administrators configure viegem_url in the platform transcription registry and a dotenvx-encrypted TINA_VIEGEM_TOKEN is injected at deployment startup (legacy database token supported only without that env); native startup decrypts its separate private env file strictly, user preferences select the backend name, and internal Bot/Desktop/dictation resolution carries only its registry-owned endpoint credential. Custom endpoints do not inherit the VieGem platform token; the browser-facing admin settings edge treats that credential as write-only. The source-build entrypoint resolves TINA_VIEGEM_DEVICE=auto to native MPS on Apple Silicon or Docker CUDA on Linux/Windows WSL2. Only the CTC model/encoder uses the GPU; FSMN and KenLM remain CPU. Actual MPS/CUDA compute and authenticated audio must pass before deployment succeeds; no silent CPU fallback. CUDA adds an owned Compose overlay with pinned cu130 wheels and one GPU reservation for inference only. MPS excludes the Docker VieGem profile and stops only the old owned CPU service before binding the same host endpoint; native startup failure attempts to restore that prior service while reporting failure. Explicit cpu remains available. Token-free Docker model-install jobs are independent of serving; native setup prepares the same pinned cache before activation. Inference mounts cached weights read-only, runtime tokens come from dotenvx and private keys are not mounted. make-down also removes/stops the owned MPS LaunchAgent. Fresh registries use VieGem. Retired Gipformer selections follow the configured default; a retired platform default moves to VieGem when available. Other preferences and foreign worker ownership are preserved. Per-account ASR runtime control keeps shared workers alive while any enabled account requests them. A derived-key authenticated drain fence refuses new requests and cannot stop a worker with active inference. CUDA hardware validation remains pending on a real NVIDIA host. VieGem has an optional operator-only bounded name prior, default zero/off; paired local name experiments do not alter production tuning without evidence.

nodes.name: desktop
nodes.description: all-in-one dev host: bot+collector+gateway in one process; capture sessions resolve central identity ASR settings once (personal API key > platform > environment), pin the selection until stop and expose credential-free backend metadata Local SQLite journal preserves confirmed ASR, PCM source timestamps and owner corrections across restarts; document/review/audio routes consult canAccess. Explicit post-meeting second-pass ASR yields persisted proposals; one worker pauses between utterances for live capture and never edits text before owner Apply.; input ring shared with ASR, per-session/source sample clock and original capture timestamp archived in SQLite; authorized audio-timeline.v1 metadata and RAM-to-archive range reads never fill missing samples; WS /ws fans out transcript.v1 confirmed/pending frames to local capture clients; vi-en pending ASR language reviews archive original/retry text plus source PCM separately from confirmed transcript; owner/origin-checked asr-reviews routes and review UI expose suggestions without adding them to canonical or memory. Ingest ready advertises recording_ack and recording_resume for an optional client_session nonce. REC1 acknowledgements follow sink processing; explicit finalization closes immediately while unexpected socket closes retain the recording assembler for 30 seconds for same-client resume. Shutdown flushes pending assemblers. Different logical client sessions finalize separately; replacing a current recording master preserves the older file as a versioned sibling. Opt-in audio_ack=sample-range.v1 requires indexed PCM and a client_session nonce; exact-range audio-ack follows durable journal insertion. Persistent archive session ids deduplicate identical PCM/timestamps across reconnect and process restart without duplicate pipeline feed; conflicting/overlapping ranges fail without ACK. Socket-local pipeline RAM stays separate from archive identity. Audio ACK does not promise downstream ASR completion. A single background ASR recovery worker resumes unprocessed source/sample ranges after stop or restart, using bounded 15-second archive windows and the existing Gmeet ASR/filter engine. It yields to live capture, retries failures with backoff, pins an opaque backend/credential digest, and never substitutes an unavailable configuration. Owner/origin-scoped asr-recovery.v1 exposes jobs and checkpoints. Recovered mixed audio stays unattributed; known channel names and local mic identity are preserved. Live confirmed segments project accepted canonical text at the gateway; drafts for edited/restored ids are suppressed. transcript.v1 binary/event shapes are unchanged and revision metadata remains on the separate transcript.revised/HTTP interfaces. Owner-only stt-foundation.v1 snapshots persist a journal instance and monotonic sequence; globally stable meeting/source/segment IDs retain exact sample references and accepted revision history. stt-metrics.v1 distinguishes bounded ASR-call, capture lag, SQLite persistence, caption and client-reported foreground UI timing; no text/audio in metrics. Mixed lane transcript IDs include connection and source channel so mic/tab/reconnect turn counters cannot collide. STT diagnostics separate confirmed-caption publication delay from draft-window age; the legacy combined series remains available. Capture teardown plans missing source/sample ranges instead of blanket-checkpointing received PCM; only confirmed or successfully committed recovery ranges advance ASR coverage. Historical checkpoints are preserved. Late accepted PCM atomically reopens completed ASR sessions before ACK so appended tails remain recoverable. Batch archive recovery selects the existing mixed media/repetition filter through the Gmeet host policy hook, retaining short single-word speech while RMS/confidence/language checks remain in force; live Gmeet defaults and completed historical jobs are unchanged. Desktop owns a meeting-local SQLite speaker registry: channel 1000 is one local microphone identity, raw 1002 is archive-only, verified Meet participant IDs bind distinct people, and system mix 999 stays unknown. Owner rename/assignment uses independent speaker revisions and the durable metadata outbox. Owner-triggered post-meeting diarization sends verified saved system audio to the existing authenticated loopback worker; proposals require explicit Apply with registry, text, timeline and audio-hash checks. Manual names/unknown and participant identities are protected. Owner-only canonical and meeting-memory endpoints share accepted speaker projection; drafts/raw mic never become evidence, and words remain segment_fallback without forced alignment. HTTP Window ASR defaults remain unchanged. Owner-triggered post-meeting MFA alignment batches up to 20 verified continuous mono PCM16 clips, at most 30 seconds each, over current accepted text. Alignment jobs yield between batches to live capture and serialize with refinement/diarization. Per-segment accepted timing publishes only after expected text revision, text/audio hashes and capture source references still match. Word audio playback rechecks provenance and never assigns time to OOV tokens. Text edits and Restore invalidate timing atomically. Canonical words/phrases use source-absolute times; speaker attribution is reprojected from the current registry and applied acoustic turns. Alignment types, hashing, validation and speaker projection live in the pure alignment-model module; transcript-journal depends on that model, while the alignment worker depends on the journal, without a runtime import cycle.

nodes.name: meeting-api
nodes.description: collector + bot-spawn + recordings + sessions + calendar import/autojoin (the hub). Calendar sync reads bounded Google Calendar event snapshots or ICS feeds; Google OAuth is read-only for Calendar, Meet and People; per-calendar auto-join defaults off. Google Meet attendance uses provider account IDs and People email resolution, never display-name matching. It optionally asks an external service authority before spawn and at one-minute active boundaries. Owns immutable raw ASR plus the transcript_edits overlay with locked expected_revision checks. Owns owner-triggered advisory RMS/clipping/quiet-frame/repetition checks over bounded saved bot audio, check-only jobs without inference, and selective refinement of flagged clips. Explicit failed-only retry carries settled proposals forward and verifies backend/model, text revision and saved audio hash; sanitized error codes describe ASR failures; original transcript remains immutable until explicit Apply. Owns post-meeting recording refinement and optional Vietnamese word alignment over clocked saved audio; alignment/OOV timestamps are a separate owner view and never rewrite transcript-document.v1 or raw ASR. Canonical accepted text/revision and alignment metadata use the transactional JSONB revision outbox; current-text GIN search remains text-only. Owns the durable meeting-local speaker registry, observed Meet participant bindings, owner-confirmed names and assignment history; owner-triggered local CPU diarization applies speaker overlays and word attribution leaves overlap/uncertainty unknown. Persists owner-only canonical-transcript.v1 with current text, source-clock word alignment, speaker attribution and hashes. Incremental meeting-memory.v1 groups finalized speech into conversation windows and exact-quote VI/EN extraction candidates, rebuilt on source revisions; no inferred owner/deadline. Owner-only stt-foundation.v1 native exports and CAS-protected read-only source replicas in meeting.data.stt_replicas retain source authority; replicas never overwrite native Bot canonical rows. Alignment commits atomically reject stale expected_revision; job admission uses expected prior job ID; raw collector upserts cannot overwrite edited rows. Content-free transcript_storage events separate PostgreSQL persistence from Redis mutable-tail queue age. Bot refinement optionally pins bounded gain for quiet clips, retaining original sample timing/hash and recording prepared-input provenance and last ASR HTTP duration. A bounded local A/B evaluation tool measures accent-preserving CER/token/boundary metrics without modifying application data. Saved bot clips preserve packet timestamps through a bounded coarse seek and trim on the 16 kHz sample clock; absent audio beyond 1 ms is rejected without padding. Apply retains prepared-input provenance in immutable correction history even after later jobs or Restore. Bot review compares Unicode-preserving repetition/non-lexical text cues with original-clip quiet-frame evidence, and checks second-pass suggestions against those same acoustics. Source and proposal checks remain advisory, revision-bound and owner-only; no speech-absence claim, automatic deletion or Apply. Authorized voice config pins each active bot owner speech profile once in private session Redis (one-day idle expiry), signs it for the TTS service and gates readiness on public-notice warmup. Account glossary data is not written into meeting projections or transcripts. Browser preview signs only bounded owner-supplied pronunciation samples and keeps service/signing keys server-side. Paused/error voice turns expose only an optional handoff hint; owner claims require ended playback and no room lease, preserve validated task fields and detach that task flow atomically. Unclaimed snapshots expire after five minutes, claimed after fifteen. Preserve typed upstream request/source conflicts separately from unknown writes. Decision-source conflicts return to clarification without an uncertain-write marker; task and decision unknown writes both prevent blind reconfirmation. Evidence-bearing Decision Flow review prompts resolve current fingerprints before queuing speech; accepted review receipts retain their source refs. Stale evidence returns to source clarification, source-service errors preserve fields without a decided claim, and Stop/policy lease checks still fence playback. Caller history retains three receipt-confirmed turns plus one pending candidate in Redis; prompts receive only three heard turns, so failed or unplayed attempts cannot evict confirmed context. Session/policy/source and stopped-prefix checks remain authoritative. Google Calendar reconciliation records per-source link/time authority and disarms revoked calendar-managed links without modifying manual/live meetings. All-day dates remain provenance-only dates with no scheduled join instant; internal calendar timezone scopes date filtering and finished-occurrence comparison. Voice source policies may reference owner-scoped project profiles; referenced rooms bypass readiness caching for revocation checks before TTS. New voice rooms select the sandbox agent backend; saved completion policies stay explicit. Backend changes use normal policy CAS/cancellation. Owner-facing join_failure_summary distinguishes a Google pre-admission block, host denial, lobby expiry and missing signed-in session using fixed copy derived from bounded evidence. List/detail responses regenerate this summary and omit it for non-owners; raw failure strings never become UI copy. Restricted transcript shares may explicitly include read-only recordings. Recipient email verification precedes redemption; recording reads recheck expiry/revocation, while uploads and deletes stay producer/owner-only. Owner-scoped annotations save a report of up to 6000 characters at data.summary, separate from the unchanged 16 KiB metadata budget. Completed artifact deletion removes data.summary and legacy metadata.tina_summary and rejects late summary writes. New Bot rows and planned rows when first claimed by a Bot, plus resumed legacy rows without a saved preference, enable canonical AI Notes by default; generation waits for terminal status and finalized transcript windows, while explicit disable remains authoritative.

nodes.description: runtime.v1 kernel: POST /workloads starts Docker, Kubernetes, or process workloads. The opt-in ECS backend launches a pinned Fargate meeting-bot task and passes the invocation through a private SSE-S3 environment file whose ARN is the only ECS override. Cron schedules carry an IANA timezone (legacy UTC); local wall-clock boundaries avoid DST arithmetic drift. nodes.name: agent-worker
nodes.description: spawned isolated workspace-agent worker; selectable Claude Code, Codex app-server, or Antigravity CLI (agy) harness; each harness dispatch mounts the ordered [_global, active workspaces, _system] stack, fails closed without _global, and loads its authoritative entry context. Groq mode reuses Codex against the fixed Groq Responses endpoint for chat and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions for meeting summaries. A per-turn Groq model profile disables unsupported freeform patch tools and namespace delegation at the CLI source, with provider-neutral TINA instructions and file edits through the existing sandboxed function tools. DeepSeek mode reuses Claude Code against DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint for chat and its Chat Completions endpoint for summaries. Gemini mode selects agy's Gemini API-key provider for chat and the Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint for summaries, without consumer/OAuth credentials or a synthetic Terms acknowledgment. Dispatch selects each effective per-user/platform key for both paths and clears other providers' credentials. A temporary authenticated loopback proxy inside the worker strips unsupported Responses fields and non-function tools, maps developer instructions to system messages for non-GPT-OSS chat templates without changing tool history, rejects known non-tool chat models, serializes function calls and preserves streamed events and HTTP errors; it never executes tools or expands the harness grants. Codex pins explicit named per-turn filesystem profiles to TINA write grants, protects agent/Git metadata and excludes temporary write roots. Trusted chat/routine turns map WebSearch/WebFetch grants to cached/live hosted web tools; untrusted event/transcription turns disable web tools and remain read-only/offline. Shell networking requires Bash plus WebFetch and a root-owned exclusive GitHub-domain proxy policy, with private addresses, upstream proxies, Unix-socket forwarding and direct-network bypass blocked. Managed networking is not globally forced so offline turns remain isolated. Codex loads workspace instructions and skills, maps TINA auto/gate MCP grants to Codex approval modes, streams tool lifecycle events, pauses gate calls for owner-scoped, one-call decisions over chat streams using tool-approval.v1, and participates in the shared transcript-size resume cap. A private per-TINA-session provider-thread index preserves display history across provider restarts; reset removes this index, and legacy recovery uses only same-subject, same-session Redis events newer than session creation. Codex user-message events define visible human messages, excluding injected environment and developer context; restored tool names remain descriptive. Antigravity maps TINA mount grants to read_file/write_file permissions, sandboxes commands, loads governed skills, exposes only auto-granted non-secret MCP servers in headless mode, and normalizes streamed events and conversation ids. The legacy Antigravity model selection requires a persisted Terms warning acknowledgment; consumer OAuth access through third-party software is prohibited by Google's terms. The Gemini API-key provider has independent credential preflight. Harness-written kg/entities files are workspace.v1-validated before commit. Post-meeting summary uses a tool-less CompletionPort and a deterministic writer with a local generated-content fingerprint, inference-time compare-and-swap, workspace locking and atomic publication; user-edited or unmarked existing documents are preserved, and only the meeting entity path is committed. Meeting Q&A uses a private short-lived, tool-less CompletionPort job with read-only mounts and no public chat history. Web-enabled Codex turns render explicit source metadata as final Markdown links and persist bounded per-turn source records in private continuity; missing citation mappings are never guessed. Explicit Knowledge research instructions create a new private Markdown note with meeting/repo/web source rows, evidence versions and verification dates, preserving other files and canonical transcript/audio. Voice jobs optionally request provider-side JSON Schema for answers/plans/review, restricted to authorized source IDs; explicit unsupported-format responses alone use the validated legacy path. Retrieval sets above eight excerpts get one optional four-second HTTP-timeout selected-model rerank, selecting up to 12 IDs plus recent/heard-history references within 32 excerpts/24000 characters. Invalid/empty rankings and oversized pinned context retain the original retrieval; verification and repair always receive the full original evidence. Ranking consumes the existing voice scheduling deadline. Content-free UUID-correlated stage logs cover selection, model calls, review and repair. Decision Flow extraction and evidence validation use the selected CompletionPort; decided evidence gets an independent existing voice verifier, never workspace tools. Voice numeric verification uses comparison-only unambiguous Vietnamese cardinal/decimal/percentage and monetary-scale facts, preserving quotes and reply text. Per-citation extraction, value/sign/unit checks and the existing semantic reviewer/repair remain required. Ambiguous spellings stay literal; the guarded LLM reranker is unchanged. A valid empty LLM rerank is a distinct no-match outcome, retaining only explicit recent/heard pins rather than the original list or automatic comparison seeds. Original evidence remains available for contradiction review; generation and repair after no-match cannot restore discarded source IDs. Valid empty answers retain retrieval_empty while real service failures are not masked. Meeting voice uses the selected HTTP CompletionPort for planning, generation and verification; CLI harnesses remain for workspace/chat turns only. Opt-in automatic public source routing uses a bounded question-only classifier without room sources/history. Partial spoken answers require independent verification of every retained claim and follow-up. Sandbox voice uses the configured CLI harness in a disposable cwd with no native tools/MCP or account workspace mounts. LangGraph executes validated source-tool proposals. The process group is bounded to remaining time and killed when the live room lease is lost. Independent CompletionPort verification still gates TTS. Voice sandbox alone opts into native structured final output: Codex turn outputSchema and Claude JSON Schema with structured_output extraction. Chat turns omit this option. Existing voice answer validators, one format repair, source review and live-turn guards remain authoritative; malformed sandbox plans get one bounded format repair with the existing tool allowlist. Exhausted answer format repairs publish generation_format_invalid separately from factual verification rejection, with owner handoff and evaluation treating it as a generation failure. Public-web outcomes distinguish absent excerpts, empty generation, numeric mismatch, semantic rejection and verifier outages. Content-free voice_web_result diagnostics retain request UUID, retrieved-source count and fixed verification/upstream error codes. LiveKit lookup and final replies preserve these categories without weakening validation or retrying providers. Public voice reuses one API-only draft repair within its existing live lease and deadline; repaired claims must pass deterministic quantities and independent semantic review before TTS. Currency comparison normalizes unambiguous grouped amounts and Vietnamese scales without rewriting sources, retains signs/currencies and separates per-lượng from per-chỉ. Ambiguous single separators without locale evidence, dates and versions stay literal. Gold-price voice extraction binds up to eight rows to exact product/amount/column/unit/update quotes and original URLs; an independent API review gates row relations before deterministic speech formatting. It shares the existing one-repair budget, public-only payload, deadline and Stop lease. Source clocks are retained, missing/old dates cannot become today, and supplier/date groups never merge buy/sell values. The staging workspace pilot pins a per-subject task revision and requires its mounted paths and write modes to match the current grants. A loopback sidecar owns the Valkey credentials and can relay only one workload stream pair. The staging post-meeting draft task runs on demand on Fargate with pinned Bedrock Nova Lite and uses bounded transcript and document excerpts, without workspace mounts or harness tools.

nodes.name: TINA Capture
nodes.description: Tauri/Rust macOS 15+ client: explicit meeting capture of microphone and system audio plus hold-to-dictate from a global Fn shortcut. Separate source channels are validated, resampled to 16 kHz with SpeexDSP and sent as capture.v1 to local Desktop. Native Capture does not link Sherpa/ONNX for resampling, avoiding incompatible KissFFT symbols between Sherpa and fixed-point Speex. Resampler float samples use PCM16 units internally and return normalized PCM; packet boundaries do not change the output waveform. Default dual-source capture uses Speex AEC plus residual echo suppression with channel 999 as far-end reference, preserves raw mic on archive-only channel 1002 and routes processed mic on channel 1000 to ASR. Aligned dual-source blocks additionally use a stateful 70 Hz high-pass on mic/reference and Speex denoising capped at -3 dB; AGC/VAD remain off and no samples are gated out. TINA_MIC_CLEANUP=0 restores AEC plus residual-only behavior; TINA_SPEEX_RESIDUAL_SUPPRESSION=0 keeps linear AEC only and TINA_SPEEX_AEC=0 uses raw mic. Capture Diagnostics distinguishes configured AEC from actual processed blocks, reports bypassed samples and source mic clipping, and exposes setup fallback reasons without audio or text. Pause/resume clears pending audio and DSP state while retaining session counters. Missing sample-index.v1, DSP initialization failure or unavailable reference passes original mic through. CoreAudio process metadata raises a non-focusable detect/record/ended overlay for allowlisted meeting apps after a 5 s sustain; capture never auto-starts, pause drops frames and freezes the elapsed clock, and a meeting-end reminder offers a 15 s keep-recording grace. Live captions subscribe to Desktop WS /ws, keep a rolling confirmed/pending window for the floating subtitle window, and never affect audio. Markdown export reads the Desktop transcript. Dictation uses microphone only; after stop, Desktop may forward only final transcript text through the authenticated polish bridge, while TINA Capture keeps raw ASR available for copy/restore and pastes raw text if polish is unavailable. No screen images or active-app contents are read; no model or service credentials are loaded in this process.

nodes.description: Local SQLite WAL: durable meetings, immutable per-source Float32 PCM timeline and original ASR with compare-and-swap correction history. Single writer Desktop. Audio cap 2 GiB/session is surfaced as archive incomplete; ASR continues. Stores refinement jobs/proposals and atomic apply with ASR model/audio hash provenance. Canonical FTS5 current-text index and transactional revision outbox, rebuilt/replayed across restart. Additive asr_language_reviews table stores pending original/retry results and Float32 request audio, deduplicated per meeting/session/PCM hash; 90-second request and 256 MiB per-meeting audio limits. Additive audio_capture_sessions maps meeting/client nonce to persistent archive id; audio_chunks acts as durable exact sample-range receipt with byte/timestamp comparison and overlap rejection. Existing 2 GiB session quota includes pre-restart bytes. Additive asr_sessions, asr_windows and asr_coverage persist routing digests, source/sample jobs and processed intervals; speaker_name is stored with audio chunks. Live confirmed text and its coverage commit atomically. Recovery transcript, FTS index, sample checkpoint and completed job share one SQLite transaction. Running jobs become retryable after process restart. Historical PCM without routing metadata is not auto-decoded. Additive journal_metadata and foundation_versions retain source authority identity and export sequence across restart. Additive speaker_registries, diarization_jobs and canonical_projections persist independent speaker revisions, source-bound proposals and canonical projection versions. Speaker updates and speaker-revision.v1 outbox commit atomically; raw PCM/text remain unchanged. Speaker-aware stt-foundation.v1 exports preserve optional speaker ID/revision. Additive alignment_jobs and alignment_results store accepted-text timing independent from raw ASR; transcript_sequences supplies monotonic metadata invalidation sequences independent of text history length. Alignment result and metadata-only event commit in one SQLite transaction. Original source timestamps and accepted/raw text never change during alignment.

nodes.description: Owner-only second-pass ASR proposals for Desktop and clocked bot recordings. Optional fixed vocabulary; explicit revision-safe Apply and immutable raw Restore. Bot refinement optionally pins bounded gain for quiet clips, retaining original sample timing/hash and recording prepared-input provenance and last ASR HTTP duration. A bounded local A/B evaluation tool measures accent-preserving CER/token/boundary metrics without modifying application data. Saved bot clips preserve packet timestamps through a bounded coarse seek and trim on the 16 kHz sample clock; absent audio beyond 1 ms is rejected without padding. Apply retains prepared-input provenance in immutable correction history even after later jobs or Restore. Bot review compares Unicode-preserving repetition/non-lexical text cues with original-clip quiet-frame evidence, and checks second-pass suggestions against those same acoustics. Source and proposal checks remain advisory, revision-bound and owner-only; no speech-absence claim, automatic deletion or Apply.

nodes.name: Optional Vietnamese TTS sidecar
nodes.description: Optional Compose or Helm service under deploy/tts: Blaze VieNeu v3 Turbo Enhanced ONNX on CPU with preset voices. Authenticated OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech consumes bounded text and returns headerless mono PCM16 at 24 kHz. Provisioning the pinned Enhanced snapshot requires Hugging Face read access. Explicit invocation meeting IDs map to projects; default-only preview and unknown meetings do not inherit another project. Clients cannot supply dictionaries. Custom preprocessing excludes code/URLs/email; no speech text is logged or saved over canonical text. Bot serializes validated answer sentences and checks policy before each sentence. HTTP failure after headers omits the chunk terminator; cancellation closes the generator between native calls while retaining bounded FIFO admission and absolute deadlines. Three-meeting operation keeps one native synthesis, six FIFO waiters, 30-second queue timeout and sixteen bounded connections. CPU threads (1-8) and bot prebuffer (80-1000 ms) are configurable; the local small-set benchmark selected four threads and retained 150 ms. Model inference is still single-flight with bounded FIFO.

Pinned ONNX/tokenizer assets and MIT notice are baked into Agent API. Whole-meeting recap intent separately covers every approved transcript chunk in chronological <=12-source/12000-character parts. Verified map facts are reduced in bounded groups, then final claims are checked against original plus related evidence. All jobs recheck current source permissions before dispatch and final release fences changes to the complete input snapshot. Recaps are read-only derived output and do not edit canonical notes/transcript. Neighbor chunks supply context under the existing budgets; final source checks regenerate the same projection and parent changes revoke every affected chunk; no embeddings or external tools. Voice drafts receive an exact digit/date citation guard and a separate selected-model entailment/contradiction review. Identity, basic social/capability requests and unsupported external actions use fixed server-owned assistant responses with no meeting fact generation. Compound/ambiguous questions remain evidence-scoped and public web stays explicit. One rejected draft may be repaired using the same approved sources and must pass both checks again; supported partial answers may ask a short follow-up. Content-free verification codes (at most two) are stored with the owner-visible reply, never drafts or reviewer prose. Provider budgets share a 50-second scheduling deadline: generation up to 25s, each review/repair up to 10s; rejected/unavailable review never releases the unchecked draft. Optional owner-selected engine=tina|livekit defaults to tina. The three-meeting self-hosted Agents runtime uses confirmed ASR questions over custom HTTP I/O and sends PCM back through the existing bot playback; raw meeting audio and canonical transcripts stay on their original path. New bots advertise bridge support; legacy bots refuse the pilot instead of silently using native voice. VoiceTurnPermit is an internal boolean reply bound to the exact current request and active bot session, requiring both owner identity and the service secret. The 360-second exclusive reservation covers the bot total 330-second wait/playback budget. The bot announces a slow whole-meeting recap once using fixed cached local TTS, waits for the background result and automatically plays only its verified final answer. Transcript capture continues and existing Stop/caller/policy/generation fences refuse late results. The 120-second recap deadline returns a source-free summary_pending failure when exhausted, with no promise of later automatic speech. Public fixed speech has three independently rotating groups per bot/meeting: name-only acknowledgments, generic question waiting and recap waiting (four phrases each). All twelve phrases are prewarmed by shared TTS and bypass the busy Agents session. Normalized exact notice echoes cannot consume caller continuation. Fast answers, including those arriving during notice authorization, omit filler; at most one waiting phrase is spoken and no LLM or unobserved web/Wiki/tool activity is invented. Capability-only GET /bots/voice/{meeting}/{session}/turn/{request}?revision confirms the exact current Redis reservation for SDK PCM. /ready replaces /health for cross-service voice admission; TTS auth/audio format must pass before a bot claims readiness. New capable Google Meet rooms now seed engine=livekit and enabled/include_transcript/allow_general_knowledge/allow_web_search=true, with NS Low on and no document grants. Manual and calendar joins resolve account preparation preferences; explicit account opt-out and saved room choices survive. Legacy model defaults remain off/native, and web still requires an explicit public query. New Compose templates configure the local Agents URL. Owner-only tool progress uses allowlisted stages, current request/session/revision and room lease; it is carried on the existing voice status read without source text. Clarification context derives only from actual heard turns for the same caller and policy; the last three turns retain the original goal and refinements while the latest clarification is fresh (30 seconds). Source fingerprints remain mandatory for historical facts. A slow question after a wake acknowledgment gets one cached waiting notice after four seconds; answer arrival, Stop and generation changes cancel delayed speech. Explicit voice action requests can use draft_task/draft_decision through the existing SDK tool loop. Proposed private workspace records require a completed readback, matching policy and authenticated meeting-owner review before exclusive workspace entity publication. Voice identity never authorizes approval; tasks remain open, decisions are owner-reviewed notes, and canonical transcript/source grants are unchanged. During THINKING, explicit same-caller refinements cancel the prior turn and await exact SDK cleanup before a fresh UUID combines the original goal with the update. Only intent is carried, not unplayed answers; public queries require explicit restatement. Atomic request/lease checks prevent old heartbeats from replacing new state. Recap waits poll the current permit every 250 ms and stop scheduling later stages after cancellation; in-flight synchronous provider work may finish but cannot authorize playback. Speaking interruptions additionally accept final same-caller soft corrections of at least three words/350 ms, exclude backchannels and recent textual playback echoes, and retain the original question for corrections. Playback is muted before confirmed sentence-prefix reporting, which precedes core cancellation; failed receipt/cancellation prevents automatic replacement. At most eight same-caller non-echo ASR hypotheses survive cancellation for quiet rearm. Partly spoken sentences remain excluded without word alignment. include_approved_actions defaults false and opt-in shares only current entity files nominated by owner-approved drafts of this meeting. search_approved_actions reads current task/decision evidence with full-file fingerprints. calculate executes bounded Decimal/calendar-day expressions from spoken or exact returned source handles; derived calculation sources bind operand fingerprints and are recomputed on finalization/inspection. No arbitrary code, inferred Friday, cross-meeting grant, canonical fact write or public-context export is introduced. shared_meeting_ids defaults empty, selects at most four other owned meeting transcripts and is owner/revision/deletion checked on Save and use. search_shared_meetings searches only that scope plus opted-in current transcript; no other-meeting documents/tasks/history are granted. Namespaced source keys and fingerprint-bound meeting identity prevent collisions; retrieval/reranking retain complementary meeting evidence and adjacent context never crosses meetings. Current-room tools and generic recaps remain current-only. Final release and owner evidence inspection reread source permissions/fingerprints; client cards link to the source meeting. Public routes remain isolated. Anchored voice source-open commands select only the same known caller's completed source-bearing answer from this session/policy within two minutes. The SDK open_source tool uses a server-selected cited handle with fresh authorization; ambiguous targets require a source ordinal. Owner-only content-free runtime navigation hints become eligible after completed acknowledgment and expire in 60 seconds. A once-claimable owner POST revalidates source access and session/policy/heartbeat before Terminal opens an existing doc or reveals the original segment. Hidden/reloaded views do not consume hints; no arbitrary URL/path, new source grant, canonical write or Extension control is introduced. Optional flow_plan/flow_apply agent operations use the existing capability/request/revision and refuse worker-supplied slot state. Task flow state is core-owned and gated by completed playback receipts. Recovery adds no_input/dialogue_paused diagnostic codes and clarification_exhausted/draft_unavailable reply reasons. Silent follow-up expiry never speaks automatically; service failures do not consume clarification attempts or authorize a new task write.

nodes.name: Optional local LiveKit Agents pilot
nodes.description: Pinned LiveKit Agents 1.8.11 worker on Compose or Helm, up to three independent rooms and AgentSessions in one process. Custom LLM adapter uses capability-scoped TINA context/plan/lookup/final-answer endpoints; Agents executes up to two native SDK batches of two read-only tools selected by the configured LLM through TINA's credential boundary; custom TTS adapter calls shared VieNeu. No owner/provider API keys or workspace mounts. Whole-meeting recap requests skip keyword tool planning and use the source-authorized TINA map/reduce/verify recap flow; raw media ownership remains in the meeting bot. Supplemental tool planning sees prior results and may rewrite a private retrieval query or read surrounding original text using a per-turn opaque handle. The core limits two plans/four attempted tools to a shared 30-second retrieval phase; timeouts skip work and retain successful queries. Context handles are current-source fingerprint-bound, source permissions are rechecked, and Stop/final dispatch fence late results. SDK ChatContext is scoped by meeting/session/policy and hashed caller (32 callers, three turns, 15-minute expiry), refreshed from TINA's source-valid actual playback receipts before every turn. Generated but unheard text is discarded. TINA matches SDK context to heard history, controls source permissions, and verifies the final reply. PCM HTTP output is bounded and carries no microphone playback receipt. Stop UUID fences, disconnect cancellation, policy reaping and 90s idle cleanup apply. Raw room audio/text inputs, room transcript outputs and recording are disabled. LLM planning/tool/final failures release the core reservation and retire the SDK runtime for a fresh next turn. Per-request synthesis completion is tracked independently of SpeechHandle; partial TTS failure aborts the HTTP PCM stream without a success terminator. Header guards use pure ASGI to preserve transport errors. Cleanup claims the exact registry generation under the opening lock and each generation has a unique room name, preventing stale/delayed deletion of a replacement. Configuration distinguishes permission/session rejection from transient service errors: 401/403/404 deny, 409 invalidates, and other non-200 responses become 503. Transient errors preserve busy/recent rooms without authorizing new requests or bypassing source checks. The TINA background recap pool retains one exclusive voice turn while SDK LLM work waits up to 160 seconds and the HTTP answer route up to 165 seconds; progress announcements bypass the busy SDK session using shared fixed-message TTS. No new audio/RAG runtime or simultaneous room question is introduced. Capacity is three meetings in one replica/process; a fourth is refused. Authenticated /ready validates local TTS token and PCM metadata without inference; full capacity is not unhealthy. SDK PCM revalidates the current Redis turn via the capability-only Meeting API before synthesis, while streaming and at completion, including after SDK runtime recreation. Automated qualification opens three actual local rooms and fifteen uncached TTS streams over TCP with explicit synthetic meeting/LLM/receipt authority. Live meeting and actual model-provider acceptance remain separate. PCM admission belongs to the complete ASGI response lifetime; header-send and early disconnect failures close the iterator and release reserved lookahead credits, preventing a room from becoming permanently audio-busy. The TTS adapter explicitly closes upstream PCM iterators on success, failure and cancellation, unwinding shared TTS HTTP connections; tests cover Stop before first audio and buffered-output cleanup. Optional TINA_LIVEKIT_AUDIO routes both continuous transcript and confirmed-question ASR through a standalone SDK STT adapter to the bot-selected ASR backend. Bounded 16 kHz PCM16 windows retain raw source offsets and Server-Timing; bot LocalAgreement and canonical writes stay unchanged. A private WebSocket applies the existing WebRTC NS Low library once before the shared ASR/Silero/KWS split, with per-channel state, exact sample counts and fail-open raw drainage. Signed capabilities pin meeting/session/backend credentials; Meeting API latest-session/Stop checks precede and follow STT and run periodically during NS. Limits are eight in-flight STT calls and eight NS connections; raw room input and automatic SDK turn endpointing remain off. New bridge-capable bots also stream accepted per-turn PCM16 frames over one private STT WebSocket. This service retains up to 32 seconds per turn and 32 turns per connection, then assembles windows referenced by turn/source timestamp/sample count and verified by PCM SHA256. Existing bot cadence/cap cuts and LocalAgreement keep canonical window/confirmation authority and a bounded local fallback copy. SDK draft results reuse original client quality/language filters. Missing cache/checksum mismatch or disconnect uses the exact authenticated HTTP window fallback; reconnect cannot accept late old-socket replies. Eight STT connections and eight in-flight requests per connection are bounded by the shared eight-call inference semaphore. Abort cancels matching SDK work; turn close/disconnect frees caches/tasks. This is continuous transport with windowed model inference, not native model streaming. Optional TINA_LIVEKIT_VAD_SHADOW reuses the exact pinned bot Silero/VadMonitor code and model from a read-only shared cache in a private per-bot VAD WebSocket. Up to eight observers retain channel-isolated state (32 channels). Only current transcribing sessions with enabled room voice can connect. The bot sends the same filtered Float32 frames, state/generation controls and content-free numeric endpoint candidates. Hosted activity/source endpoints and ASR coverage are compared without question text or names. Local KWS/lexical/quiet/question authority stays unchanged; observer failures/disagreement cannot affect transcript or answer dispatch. A separate ready boolean reports observer asset readiness without failing core STT/TTS health. TINA_AUDIO_DENOISER selects exactly one preprocessing engine (webrtc default or local DTLN). DTLN uses two immutable upstream ONNX models with size/SHA256 and MIT notice verified at image build; inference is offline CPU with shared read-only model sessions and independent per-channel LSTM/overlap state. 128-sample hops and 384-sample delay compensation reuse the exact-count frame adapter; original 64 ms capture/source clocks and partial tails are retained. Fixed 50-percent aligned dry/wet mix protects initial speech quality; no extra high-frequency rolloff or stacked denoiser is added. Selected model readiness is exposed as bounded metadata through owner Settings without forwarding TTS/provider credentials. Runtime filter failure retains the existing exact-once original-PCM fallback. Provider tool plans use per-tool argument schemas shared with the Agent domain: search text, context/source handles, draft requests, arithmetic expressions or explicit date pairs. Shared JSON Schema validation normalizes typed arguments to existing bounded name/query HTTP/Redis calls; legacy query-format plans remain accepted. Dependent/mixed/calculation/context/navigation/draft/public-web batches remain sequential. Graph assessment distinguishes found/empty/unavailable local reads: committed temporary failures consume budget but retain the lease, partial success proceeds only through TINA verified finalization, and no successful evidence after failure ends as service unavailable without answer dispatch. Core independently enforces the no-evidence service-failure gate. Content-free lookup outcomes diagnose these paths. Core records completions/executions in original plan order. Batch wall timings are separate from overlapping per-tool spans. Stop/disconnect cancels the current node. The old SDK function-tool loop is removed for these turns. Local content-free graph total/plan/per-tool/answer spans reuse the Agent voice trace helper and carry request/span UUIDs, bounded round/source counts and cancellation status. They join existing retrieval/generation/verification and bot answer/acknowledgment timing without copying questions, quotes or tokens. No graph checkpoint or external LangSmith trace is enabled; only verified final text is streamed to Agents/TTS, and current Meeting API progress continues to reach clients.
